what: Rotate PDF turns the pages of a PDF by 90 or 180 degrees and saves the result. You can turn every page, or only the pages you list.

It is perfect for scans that came out sideways or upside down, for a single landscape table inside a portrait document, or for phone photos saved in the wrong direction. The rotation is saved in the file, so the pages open the right way in every PDF reader.
The file is changed inside your browser and is not uploaded.
uses: Turn pages that were scanned in the wrong direction so they read normally.
Rotate 180 degrees when a page was fed into the scanner the wrong way.
Rotate only the page with a wide table or chart, and leave the rest as they are.
Make sure every page faces the right way before you send the file to someone else.
tutorial: Click "Click or drop a PDF here" or drag a PDF onto the box. The tool shows the file name and page count, for example "scan.pdf · 6 pages".
"90° clockwise" turns pages a quarter turn to the right. "90° counter-clockwise" turns them a quarter turn to the left. "180° (upside down)" turns them halfway around.
Leave "Pages (leave empty for all)" empty to rotate every page. To rotate only some, type them with commas and hyphens, for example 2, 5-7.
A green message such as "Rotated 3 pages" appears, with the size of the new file.
Click "Download PDF". The file is named like scan-rotated.pdf.
Each click starts again from your original file, so clicking twice does not turn pages twice. If the direction was wrong, pick another option and click "Rotate PDF" again.
features: 90 degrees clockwise, 90 degrees counter-clockwise, or 180 degrees.
Rotate the whole file, or only the pages you list.
Only the page direction changes. Text, images and links stay exactly as they were.
The rotation is always applied to the original file, so you can try different directions without stacking turns.
If a page was already rotated in the PDF, the new turn is added to it correctly.

example.title: Worked example: one sideways table in a report
example.text: Mei has a 10-page report where page 4 is a wide table that shows sideways. She loads report.pdf, chooses "90° counter-clockwise" and types 4 in the pages box. She clicks "Rotate PDF" and sees "Rotated 1 page". When she opens report-rotated.pdf, page 4 reads normally and the other nine pages are unchanged.

tips: Not sure which way to turn? Try "90° clockwise" first. If it is wrong, choose "90° counter-clockwise" and click again. The tool always starts from the original.
To fix several pages that need different turns, rotate one group, download, then load the new file and rotate the next group.
Rotating does not change the file size in any noticeable way.
Use the same page format as Split PDF: 1-3 for a range and commas between items.
problems: A message says a page "is outside this PDF"
You typed a page number larger than the page count. Check the count shown after the file loads.
The pages turned the wrong way
Choose the other 90 degree option and click "Rotate PDF" again. You do not need to reload the file.
A message says the file "is password protected"
Remove the password in a PDF reader that knows it, save a copy, and rotate that copy.
My PDF viewer still shows the old direction
Make sure you opened the downloaded file (ending in -rotated.pdf), not the original.
